reason: The narrative is told from a third-person omniscient historical perspective focused on elite actors: royalty (Athaliah, Jehosheba, Joash), religious leadership (Jehoiada the priest), military commanders (שָׂרֵ֣י הַמֵּא֗וֹת - captains of hundreds), and palace officials. While common people (עַם־ הָאָרֶץ) are mentioned as observers who rejoice, the story centers on royal succession, priestly authority, and palace intrigue. The narrative provides access to the thoughts and actions of these elite figures but not to the perspective or consciousness of ordinary working people. Regular people serve as background participants rather than the narrative's perspective.
